label: spine-lem-the-intersection-of-a-nonempty-set-is-a-set
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN
BOUNDARY: Checked the excluded empty-family case (x=∅ would make the class a proper class, but the hypothesis x≠∅ prevents this), singleton x (c_B = B, which is the intersection), x containing ∅ (forces intersection ∅, and c_B = ∅), families with disjoint members (intersection ∅, again c_B = ∅), and the general case where the intersection is nonempty. All such cases are correctly handled by the Separation argument on an arbitrarily chosen B∈x. No counterexample to the claim was found; the proof is valid for every nonempty set x in ZFC.
SOURCES: All four cited items supplied in the dispatch were inspected—def-axiom-schema-of-separation, def-axiom-of-extensionality, thm-the-empty-set-exists-and-is-unique, and def-subset-and-proper-subset. Each is accurately paraphrased in the proof’s fact labels and supports exactly the use made of it.
CHECKED: The title, the public statement, every numbered step (1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1), and the absence of a Remarks section were read and verified for mathematical accuracy and logical validity.
